title: Introduce attention handoff batcher and fused-rotary optimizer
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes:
- Adds a streaming->batch handoff path to improve continuous batching efficiency for mixed-latency workloads.
- Integrates rotary application into the fused QKV microkernel to reduce memory bandwidth and CPU overhead.
- Provides config knobs and telemetry for tuning handoff thresholds and observing KV cache resonance.
description:
Context and motivation: Production workloads with mixed short and long queries suffer from suboptimal continuous batching: short streaming requests force the runtime to flush batches frequently while long-context requests underutilize GPU windows. This PR implements an "attention handoff batcher" (AHB) that can dynamically migrate in-flight tokens from the low-latency streaming path into a throughput-optimized batching path mid-request, reducing token duplication and improving GPU utilization. Additionally, we introduce a fused-rotary optimizer that applies rotary embeddings inside the QKV microkernel, eliminating an extra memory pass and improving cache locality.

Summary of changes and commits: commit a3f1d9b - add AHB control plane and API hooks; commit 5e2b4f1 - implement handoff enqueue/dequeue state machine; commit c7d4aa6 - fused-rotary microkernel (CUDA + fallback CPU path) and unit tests; commit d1a6e42 - KV cache resonance tracking and metrics; commit e4f9b77 - add tuning flags, docs, and canary harness; commit f2c8d33 - integration tests and perf benchmarks; commit 9b7a1c0 - address review comments and stabilize CI.

Changed areas (high level): runtime/worker/streaming_batcher.cpp - new handoff coordinator and state machine; runtime/gpu/kernels/qkv_fused_rotary.cu - fused rotary + qkv GEMM path with reduced memory copies; runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.h - public knobs for handoff thresholds; runtime/kv_cache/resonance_tracker.{cpp,h} - lightweight telemetry for cache hit patterns; tools/perf/canary/attn_handoff_bench.py - new benchmarks for mixed workloads; docs/ops/handbook/attn-handoff.md - operational guidance and tuning. Smaller touches: updated logging, added feature flag redwood.experimental.attn_handoff, and new metrics redwood.attn.handoff.seconds and redwood.attn.kv.resonance.

Design notes: The AHB is conservative by default. When a streaming request matches criteria (estimated length > L and observed inter-token spacing < T), the request is marked eligible and its partial KV is checkpointed into a hot lane. The handoff happens only when the batcher has sufficient headroom, otherwise the streaming path continues. This avoids increased P99 for small interactive queries while allowing long-context work to be aggregated. The fused-rotary kernel consumes prepacked QKV tiles and applies rotary rotations inline during the GEMM accumulate to eliminate an intermediate transpose+apply step. CPU fallback keeps parity for Private deployments without CUDA.

Benchmarks and canary results: Microbenchmarks on p4d (fp16) with a mixed workload (60% short interactive, 40% long streaming) show: median latency for interactive queries unchanged (+0-2ms), P95 latency improved by ~6% on steady state, end-to-end throughput increase of 1.25x for long-context tail when handoff is enabled. For long-only synthetic traces, fused-rotary reduces overall token compute time by 12-18% and memory bandwidth by ~22% relative to the baseline rotary-then-qkv pipeline. Canary in prod-like cluster (dedicated pool) over 48h: sustained 11% lower GPU utilization for equivalent QPS and no increase in error budgets.

Testing: Unit tests added for the AHB state transitions and kernel correctness; integration tests exercise handoff under race conditions; perf harness simulates token inter-arrival distributions to validate handoff thresholds. CI: initial lint/test run failed due to a nondeterministic gating test; fixed by introducing a deterministic RNG seed in tests. Final CI status: pass across linux-cuda, linux-cpu-fallback, and e2e-canary.

Review conversation (selected): Reviewer Evan Brooks: "Nice isolation of the handoff state machine. Can you add metrics for handoff success/failure reasons?" Author (Sofia): "Added redwood.attn.handoff.reason and exported counts for each code path in resonance_tracker." Reviewer Lina Moretti: "The fused kernel looks promising — did you validate fp32/amp stability?" Author: "Yes, ran numeric diffs for fp32, fp16 (amp), and bfloat on CI; diffs are within acceptable tolerance and have regression alerts tied to the eval harness." Reviewer Priya Shah: "Concern about config complexity for ops teams." Author: "Default flags are safe; docs/ops/handbook/attn-handoff.md includes step-by-step tuning and suggested thresholds. We also added canary templates in tools/perf for ops validation." Review status: approved by Evan and Lina after two rounds, Priya approved after docs update.

Operational notes and rollout plan: Feature gated behind redwood.experimental.attn_handoff. Rollout strategy: 1) internal canary on dedicated cluster, 2) opt-in beta with selected customers (SRE/SE assist), 3) gradual ramp by percentage with automated SLO checks. Toggle knobs: handoff.enable (bool), handoff.min_estimated_len (int), handoff.max_wait_ms (int), handoff.batch_min_tokens (int). Telemetry to watch: redwood.attn.handoff.count, redwood.attn.handoff.latency, redwood.attn.kv.resonance.ratio, GPU_util_by_pool.

Backward compatibility and fallback: If the fused kernel fails (unsupported compute capability or runtime error), runtime falls back to the previous rotary+qkv flow; handoff coordinator gracefully disables for that model variant. Breaking change: none.

Merge outcome and follow-ups: Merged via squash-merge after approvals and green CI. Follow-up work tracked as ENG-8602 (automated threshold tuning) and ENG-8639 (extend fused kernel to cache-friendly int8 paths). Action items captured in PR: add more diagnostic traces for rare handoff abort reasons, and run longer 7-day canaries on high-variance workloads.

Notes for reviewers of history: This PR intentionally keeps the handoff policy simple; future iterations should explore ML-driven handoff predicates and tighter coupling with KV cache eviction heuristics.
